title: Most Vowels in a Fixed Window
statement:
You get a lowercase string s and an integer k. Look at every substring of exactly k consecutive characters.

Return the largest number of vowels any of them contains. The vowels are a, e, i, o and u.

examples.why: "ogra" and "ammi" each hold 2 vowels; no window of 4 holds 3.
There are no vowels at all ("y" does not count).
The window is the whole string: a, i and e.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Recounting each window from scratch costs k per window. What changes between two neighbouring windows?
Sliding one step right adds one character and drops one character. Only those two can change the count.
Count the first window, then for each step add 1 if the new character is a vowel and subtract 1 if the dropped one was. Track the maximum.

explain.intuition:
Two neighbouring windows share k − 1 characters. So instead of recounting, keep a running count: when the window slides right, the character that enters may add a vowel and the one that leaves may remove one. Each step costs O(1).

It is the same bookkeeping as a rolling "last k events" counter in a UI metric: increment for what comes in, decrement for what falls out.
steps: Count vowels in s[0 … k−1]; that is both the running count and the best so far.
For i from k to n − 1: add 1 if s[i] is a vowel, subtract 1 if s[i − k] is a vowel.
Update the best after each step.
Return the best. You may stop early once it reaches k.
pitfalls: Dropping s[i − k + 1] instead of s[i − k]. That keeps a window of k − 1 characters.
Forgetting to compare the very first window against the best before sliding.

solutions.title: Recount every window
solutions.idea: For each start, count vowels in the next k characters.

solutions.title: Sliding window count
solutions.idea: Keep the vowel count of the current window; each slide adds the entering character and removes the leaving one.

followups: Return the start index of the first best window as well.
The window may have any length up to k, and you want the highest share of vowels. Does a fixed window still work?
lcTitle: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
